question: to the Commission Tamás Deutsch (PfE), Csaba Dömötör (PfE), Enikő Győri (PfE), András László (PfE), Pál Szekeres (PfE) Subject:

According to publicly available information, Hungarian influencer István Szakács was arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist offence after publishing a video in which he stated that, if former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán were arrested, up to 500 000 people would march to secure his release.1 The case has raised concerns about the protection of freedom of expression. Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union (TEU) establishes the EU’s values, including democracy, the rule of law and respect for human rights. Article 11 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union guarantees freedom of expression, and Article 52(1) thereof requires that any limitation on fundamental rights be lawful, necessary and proportionate. In the light of these provisions: 1.
Has the Commission assessed whether the arrest and prosecution of István Szakács are compatible with Article 11 of the Charter and Articles 2 and 6 TEU?

Does the Commission consider the use of terrorism-related charges in response to political speech, in the absence of clear evidence of incitement to or preparation of imminent violence, compatible with Article 52(1) of the Charter?
If criminal law is being used disproportionately to restrict freedom of expression, what measures will the Commission take to ensure compliance with EU fundamental rights standards?

answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.9.2026) Freedom of expression is protected by Article 11 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU1 and the Commission is committed to ensuring its respect within the remit of its competences. However, the Commission does not intervene in individual cases. It is for Member States, including their judicial authorities, to ensure that fundamental rights are effectively respected and protected, in accordance with their national law and international human rights obligations. The Commission is therefore not in a position to assess or comment on the individual case described.
1 Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, OJ C 326, 26.10.2012, pp. 391–407.
